plan:
# Experiment Design - Does Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting Improve LLM-Agent Task-Solving in WorkArena++?

This is a design-only deliverable. Nothing has been executed and no measurements are reported. Every concrete number that depends on an unverified assumption is flagged inline as [assumption X / pending confirmation].

## A. Research Question and Operational Hypotheses

Research question (operational). Within a fixed agent stack and a fixed base LLM, does inserting explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning immediately before action emission improve task-solving on WorkArena++?

| # | Hypothesis | Test direction | One-line pre-registered decision rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 (primary, headline) | CoT (C1) greater than No-CoT (C0) on paired task-level success rate. | one-sided, delta greater than 0 | Declare C1 improves over C0 iff (i) Wilcoxon signed-rank p less than or equal to alpha after Holm-Bonferroni, (ii) paired delta greater than 0, and (iii) its 95% bootstrap CI excludes 0 with at least 80% of resampled mass above 0. |
| H1c (co-primary) | C1 greater than C0 on cost-adjusted success (success per 1k total tokens). | one-sided, delta greater than 0 | Same template as H1, applied to the second metric in the same Holm family. Two co-primaries are reported; a disagreement is narrated by tier-stratified delta and a dominance plot, not by gating them. |
| H2 (secondary) | C2 (Few-shot CoT, k=3) differs from C1. | two-sided | Report sign, magnitude, and Holm-adjusted p; the narrative question is whether few-shot exemplars add, subtract, or match zero-shot CoT. |
| H3 (secondary) | C3 (Self-consistency, N=5, T=0.7) differs from C1. | two-sided | Report sign, magnitude, and Holm-adjusted p; the narrative question is whether the five-times token spend yields a measurable success gain over C1. |

Holm family for primary inference equals {H1, H1c, H2, H3}. A pre-registered dominance plot (delta success on x-axis, delta cost-adjusted score on y-axis, one point per tier) is the canonical visual for telling the success-vs-cost story.

## B. Platform - WorkArena++ Tier Taxonomy

WorkArena++ is assumed to be the BrowserGym-served ServiceNow benchmark. The exact tier list is ratified-by-researcher and pending confirmation; no specific task IDs from the suite are used in this design.

Adopted candidate tier list (the design treats these as parameters to be locked pre-execution):

| Tier code | Candidate name | Example capability | Sample-size stratum |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | list / lookup | read-only retrieval on ServiceNow records | small-to-mid |
| T2 | search / navigation | multi-page traversal, filter/sort | mid |
| T3 | forms | create or edit record via form fields | mid |
| T4 | configuration | change system settings or workflows | small |
| T5 | composite or plan | multi-step, cross-page objectives | small (hardest) |

If the ratified list differs, the only knob that must change is per-tier sample allocation in Section H; everything downstream is tier-symbolic. Counters external to the design are revisited once the ratified tier set is in hand.

## C. Agent Stack

Base LLM. Single fixed chat model across all cells. Default proposal, pending confirmation of API access and pinning: a current frontier chat model in the GPT-4o or Claude-3.5-Sonnet class with at least 128k context, function- or tool-calling disabled (WorkArena++ uses a discrete action enum, not tool calls). The exact model id is pinned in a single model.lock file before execution and never changed mid-run. All four cells C0, C1, C2, C3 use that same id.

BrowserGym / ServiceNow. BrowserGym (release: assumption - use the most recent stable BrowserGym that ships with the adopted WorkArena++; pending confirmation) over headless Chromium controlling a ServiceNow Personal Developer Instance or shared testing tenant. Assumption: one instance per worker; instance snapshot id is fixed. UI locale: en-US (see Section L).

Observation to prompt interface.
- Page observation equals pruned HTML accessibility tree, capped at about 6k tokens.
- Action format equals BrowserGym's discrete enum.
- Prompt payload per step is a tuple of system, goal, observation tree, last action, last error, and chat history of (thought, action, observation) tuples. History is windowed to the last K turns (K=10 by default).

CoT insertion slot. A single think-block immediately before the action, channel-separated and logged verbatim for failure-mode coding (Section E).

Length-control mechanism. All four cells are constrained to a per-step output budget of at most 192 tokens total (think plus action), enforced by a stop sequence and a downstream parser. The Section G ablation explicitly tests what happens when this cap is doubled.

Decoding settings.

| Cell | Temperature | Top-p | Number of samples | Aggregation | Seed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C0 No-CoT | 0 | 1.0 | 1 | n/a | fixed |
| C1 Zero-shot CoT | 0 | 1.0 | 1 | n/a | fixed |
| C2 Few-shot CoT | 0 | 1.0 | 1 | n/a | fixed |
| C3 Self-consistency | 0.7 | 1.0 | 5 | majority action (think discarded) | fixed, plus per-sample index |

Prompt template skeleton (literal slots). Slots R and F are the only differences across cells; everything else is identical.

SYSTEM:
You are an agent controlling a ServiceNow instance. You observe an accessibility tree, you think if asked, and you emit exactly one BrowserGym action. Never exceed 192 output tokens.

GOAL: {goal}
OBSERVATION: {ax_tree}
LAST_ACTION: {last_action}
LAST_ERROR: {last_error}

R is the reasoning-instruction block (differs per cell).
F is the exemplar block (only present in C2).

NOW EMIT ONE ACTION.

R per cell:

- C0: Plan in one short sentence, then act. This is a no-reasoning filler to match verbosity.
- C1: Think step by step about the goal and the current page before acting.
- C2: inherits C1 R, exact same text.
- C3: inherits C1 R, exact same text; only temperature and N change.

F per cell:

- C0: none.
- C1: none.
- C2: k=3 worked think-action-observation exemplars drawn from the same tier, disjoint from the test set (see Section D).
- C3: none (no exemplars; reasoning sampled 5 times).

C4 (tool-augmented scratchpad) is included only if its R can be length-matched to C1 within plus or minus 10 percent of output-token expectation on a 50-step dry run; otherwise it is dropped from the run. The design is built so C4 can be added or removed without touching anything else.

## D. Protocol

Trials per task times cell: 3 (absorbs stochasticity for paired tests). Median of 3 trials is the task score. Max steps per trial: 25 (T5: 40). Wall-clock timeout per trial: 10 min. Per-step HTTP timeout: 30 s. Retry policy inside a trial: none. Trial rerun on infra error: at most 1, flagged. Environment reset: hard rollback to a known post-login snapshot before every trial; verified by a sentinel element. Randomization: Latin-square ordering of cells across tasks. Exemplar pool (C2): 5 held-out exemplar tasks per tier, disjoint from test tasks by construction. Exemplar sampling per trial: k=3 drawn without replacement from the tier pool, randomized per trial but pool is fixed. Seed hygiene: Python, NumPy, the LLM SDK, and BrowserGym are all seeded; seeds are logged per trial.

Exemplar-pool disjointness rule (C2). The exemplar pool is constructed once, before any test task is sampled, by selecting 5 demonstration tasks per tier from the WorkArena++ training portion or, if the suite does not ship a train/test split, from a frozen carve-out. The test task set is then drawn strictly disjoint from this pool by id. A single-bit audit (exemplar-in-test-set leads to run abort) is in CI before any result is reported. This guarantees C2 cannot leak task content into the test set.

## E. Metrics

| Metric | Tier | Definition | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| success | primary (H1) | Indicator that the trial reached the task's terminal done with the success predicate true on the post-condition check. Per trial; median of 3 per task times cell. | 0/1 |
| delta_success | primary | Paired (task-level) C1 minus C0 on the median-success-per-task summary. | proportion points |
| cost-adjusted score | co-primary (H1c) | success per 1,000 total tokens (input plus output, summed over the whole trial). | 1 per 1k tok |
| delta_cost-adjusted | co-primary | Paired C1 minus C0 on cost-adjusted score. | 1 per 1k tok |
| steps | secondary | Median steps-to-success over the 3 trials; for failed trials equals max_steps plus 1 (censored). | int |
| tokens_in | secondary | Sum of prompt tokens across all turns in a trial. | tokens |
| tokens_out | secondary | Sum of completion tokens across all turns in a trial. | tokens |
| dollar per success | secondary | (tokens_in times cost_in plus tokens_out times cost_out) divided by success. | USD |
| latency | secondary | Wall-clock seconds per trial and per step. | s |
| hallucination rate | secondary | Per-trial indicator that any step's think references a UI element not in the ax-tree. | 0/1 |
| loop rate | secondary | Per-trial indicator of at least 2 consecutive identical state-action pairs. | 0/1 |
| failure-mode code | secondary | One of 6 codes, labelled on every failed trial (taxonomy below). | categorical |
| Brier on done-confidence | secondary | Agent emits a 0 to 1 done-confidence before each done action; Brier equals mean of (confidence minus actual_success) squared. Instruction is identical across cells. | score |

Failure-mode taxonomy (6 codes). A failed trial is assigned exactly one code by manual review, with the think log as primary evidence. The codes are: wrong_goal (agent misinterpreted the instruction); hallucinated_element (agent referenced a UI element not in the ax-tree); action_format_error (agent emitted a malformed action); loop (agent repeated the same state-action); premature_stop (agent called done before goal was achieved); post_condition_check_failed (agent thought it was done but the predicate failed). Inter-rater reliability is reported for the subset double-coded by a second human; agreement target is Cohen kappa at least 0.7. If a judge LLM is the second coder (allowed only at this auditing step), the prompt is fixed and its outputs are reported alongside kappa to keep evaluator bias visible.

## F. Controls and Confounders

Prompt length as free parameter. C0 is given a matched-verbosity filler ("Plan in one short sentence, then act"). Output cap (192 tok) is identical across cells. A length-matched sub-analysis in Section G explicitly swaps CoT for filler to test whether any effect survives.

CoT leakage into C0 (instruction artefact). Canary task: 10 atomically-short look-up tasks are run with C0's prompt but with C1's literal R block pasted in verbatim. If the canary shows greater than 2 pp drift vs. plain C0, the architecture leaks and the design quarantines those 10 tasks out of H1 inference.

Temperature drift between deterministic cells. C0, C1, C2 all run at T=0; only C3 switches to T=0.7. The cost of C3 is recorded separately and is not silently averaged into the headline.

Tool or capability parity. All cells use the same BrowserGym action enum; function-calling, retrieval, and web search are disabled across the board.

Caching. LLM call-side caching is disabled; static prompt-template caching on the client side is enabled. Each trial's exact tokens are re-counted in post-processing.

Prompt-version pinning. Every prompt template is stored under a versioned path. The execution harness refuses to start if the loaded prompt's date stamp differs from the one in model.lock. No mid-run edits are permitted.

Exemplar-pool identity. Frozen before any test task is sampled (Section D).

Order effects. Latin square across cells within each task. First-trial contamination is tested as a covariate in Section G.

Random seed reproducibility. All RNGs seeded and logged per trial; failure to reproduce a trial from logs is itself a logged event.

## G. Analysis Plan

Statistical unit. The task. One observation per task times cell is the median of 3 trials.

Pairing. Every task sees every cell (within-subject). Pairing is therefore at the task level.

Primary test family.

- H1 (success delta): Wilcoxon signed-rank, one-sided C1 greater than C0; tiebreaker McNemar on per-trial success counts.
- H1c (cost-adjusted delta): Wilcoxon signed-rank, one-sided C1 greater than C0; tiebreaker paired bootstrap on the score.
- H2 (C2 vs C1): Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-sided; tiebreaker paired bootstrap.
- H3 (C3 vs C1): Wilcoxon signed-rank, two-sided; tiebreaker paired bootstrap.

Multiple-comparison correction. Holm-Bonferroni across {H1, H1c, H2, H3} at family-wise alpha equals 0.05.

Effect sizes. Cohen's d for paired proportions on the per-task median scores; Cliff's delta as the non-parametric backup. 95% bootstrap CIs on delta with 10,000 resamples (task-resampling preserves within-task pairing).

Disagreement-narration rule (H1 vs H1c). When H1 and H1c disagree, the headline paragraph narrates this using tier-by-tier delta tables, the dominance plot (Section A), and the numeric spend ratio equals median tokens(C1) divided by median tokens(C0). No claim of improvement is made on H1c alone if H1 fails; each is reported with its own corrected p-value.

Stratified breakdown by tier. A tier times cell interaction test (Friedman-style over tasks within tier, block by cell) is the primary heterogeneity report.

Ablations (pre-registered).

- A1 few-shot count k in {1, 3, 5}: exemplar dose-response on success and on token cost.
- A2 prompt-length-matched sub-analysis: replace C1's think block with same-length filler before action.
- A3 output-cap doubling (192 to 384 tok): whether CoT was cap-limited.
- A4 drop C4 (or include if length-matchable): tool-augmented scratchpad cost/value, only if Section C gate passes.
- A5 calibration volume check (Brier): whether identical done-confidence instruction produces non-degenerate confidences in all cells.

Robustness replications. A 10 percent subsample of tasks is re-run from scratch with fresh seeds per cell; the headline deltas are recomputed. A successful replication requires the original delta direction to hold on the subsample.

## H. Power and Sample-Size - Planning Sketch

Sample-size philosophy. Because no run has been executed, this is a planning sketch that is contingent on assumption Z1 (pending confirmation): per-tier task counts once the Section B tier list is ratified. The design treats tiers as stratifying blocks; sample-size allocation is proportional to tier difficulty (T5 gets the most trials per task because expected variance is largest there), with a floor of 20 tasks per tier for the headline contrasts.

Closed-form power for paired delta success. Treating each task's median outcome as a Bernoulli with per-cell success probability p_i, the effective paired test on n tasks has detection power roughly governed by:
- effect delta equals 7 pp (assumption Z2: planning target in the 5 to 10 pp band; pending confirmation that this is realistic for the chosen model).
- baseline proportion p_0 about 0.5 (assumption Z3: planning target; pending confirmation by a pre-registered pilot).
- sd of delta about sqrt(2 p_0 (1-p_0) - 2 rho sqrt(p_0 q_0 p_1 q_1)) with rho about 0.6 (assumption Z4: high within-task correlation under matched-pairs).
- alpha equals 0.05 after Holm over 4 tests, giving per-comparison alpha about 0.0127.
- power target 0.80.

Under these assumptions, a normal-approximation calculation gives n about 60 tasks per tier for the H1 contrast, and about 80 per tier if rho drops to 0.4. The 10 percent robustness replication borrows no power; it is run on top of n.

Per-tier allocation (planning).

| Tier | Planned tasks (n) | Why |
|---|---|---|
| T1 list/lookup | 40 | low variance ceiling; smaller n suffices |
| T2 search/navigation | 60 | nominal |
| T3 forms | 60 | nominal |
| T4 configuration | 60 | nominal; expect lower p_0 so delta detection harder |
| T5 composite or plan | 80 | higher variance, headroom for ceiling effects |
| Total | about 300 tasks | across cells times 3 trials yields about 3600 trials |

These n's are placeholders. The locked pre-execution document replaces them with the actual flowing numbers once the task pool sizes are known.

On the choice of delta equals 7 pp as a planning target. No prior-paper magnitudes or task-id-specific numbers are cited because they are not verifiable from the supplied workspace. The 7 pp band is a planning convenience that is plausibly detectable with n about 60 tasks per tier, paired; if model-level variance is much lower (a high-performing model), a 3 pp delta becomes detectable with the same n; if much higher, the design accepts lower power on smaller delta and reports it as a statistical-conclusion threat in Section I.

## I. Threats to Validity (each tied to a mitigation already in the design)

- Construct - CoT leak from prompt scaffold into C0 (instruction artefact): Mitigated by the C0 canary task (Section F), which flags any drift greater than 2 pp; affected tasks are quarantined.
- Construct - Improvement conflates success with cost: Mitigated by treating delta_success and delta_cost-adjusted score as both pre-registered co-primaries (Section A); tier breakdown shows where they disagree.
- Internal - Task-content leakage from C2 exemplars into test tasks: Mitigated by exemplar pool built before the test set and verified disjoint by id (Section D); canary audit runs in CI.
- Internal - First-trial contamination from random seeding: Mitigated by Latin square per task (Section D); first trial of session is a covariate in Section G.
- Internal - Infrastructure flakiness mistaken for agent failure: Mitigated by trial rerun policy (Section D) that flags infra errors distinctly from LLM-side failures.
- Internal - Verbosity confounded with reasoning presence: Mitigated by identical output token cap across cells, matched-verbosity filler in C0, and A2 length-matched sub-analysis (Section G).
- External - One model, one prompt template: Mitigated only by being documented as a Section L limitation; out of scope to fix without a model-times-condition design that quadruples compute.
- External - ServiceNow or BrowserGym version drift across runs: Mitigated by pinning BrowserGym and WorkArena++ versions in model.lock (Section C).
- External - en-US locale only: Documented in Section L.
- Statistical conclusion - Multiple comparisons across 4 hypotheses: Mitigated by Holm-Bonferroni across {H1, H1c, H2, H3} (Section G).
- Statistical conclusion - Non-normality of paired delta on small per-tier n: Mitigated by Wilcoxon as primary, Cliff's delta as non-parametric backup, and bootstrap CIs.
- Statistical conclusion - Calibration metric non-identifiability if done-confidence prompt is not actually attended to: Mitigated by A5 explicitly checking all cells emit non-degenerate confidences before any Brier comparison.
- Statistical conclusion - Pilot-derived p_0 assumption wrong by a wide margin: Mitigated by recomputing power from a small pilot (10 tasks) before main run and re-allocating n if needed.

## J. Feasibility and Compute

Token-volume order-of-magnitude estimate (assumption Z5, pending confirmation), per trial:
- prompt input per step about 4000 tokens (assumption);
- output per step: C0 about 50 tok, C1 and C2 about 170 tok, C3 about 170 tok times 5 samples equals 850 tok (assumption);
- steps per trial: median about 10, max 25.

Per-trial tokens about 40,000 in plus 500 to 1700 out. Per-trial spend is dominated by input; the C0 versus C1 token-ratio is about 1.0 to 1.04x. C3 multiplies output about five times, but output is small relative to input.

Total budget sketch (using Section H n equals 300 tasks, 3 trials, 4 cells).

| Cell | Trials | Approximate output tokens total | Approximate input tokens total |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | 900 | about 0.5 M | about 36 M |
| C1 | 900 | about 1.5 M | about 36 M |
| C2 | 900 | about 1.5 M | about 36 M |
| C3 | 900 | about 7.5 M | about 36 M (output times 5 dominates spend) |

Assumption Z6, pending confirmation: at an indicative frontier-model rate of about 5 USD per Mtok in and about 15 USD per Mtok out, total wall spend across all four cells is on the order of low-to-mid single-digit USD-thousands. This is a planning sketch whose numeric values are explicitly dependent on Z5 and Z6.

ServiceNow / BrowserGym provisioning. 24 CPU cores means run 24 BrowserGym jobs in parallel (one BrowserGym worker per ServiceNow PDI or shared-tenant snapshot). One ServiceNow tenant per worker avoids cross-instance interference; a pre-execution fixture script snapshots the post-login state and is replayed before every trial (Section D).

Time budget (assumption Z7). Average wall-clock per trial about 2 to 5 min (assumption, pending pilot). With 24 parallel workers and about 3600 trials, the run completes in roughly 5 to 13 hours of wall time. The bottleneck is BrowserGym rendering latency, which limit-parallelism gives directly.

Excluded from the budget: human-labour for failure-mode coding (about 300 to 900 failed trials expected; coded by 1 reviewer plus audit sub-sample) is a small, separate cost.

## K. Pre-Registration Checklist

- Fixed (locked before any execution): the four cells C0, C1, C2, C3 and their literal prompt slot diffs (Section C); the output cap; the tier list (Section B); the exemplar-pool disjointness rule and audit; the primary test family plus Holm over {H1, H1c, H2, H3}; the co-primary endpoint set; the canary task design; the seed policy; the LLM id pinned in model.lock.
- Fixed plus subject to pilot-driven n adjustment: per-tier sample-size n (Section H); the pilot recomputes power and is the only path by which n can change.
- Fixed plus conditional: including C4 (tool-augmented scratchpad) only if Section C length-match passes; otherwise C4 is dropped, not approximated.
- Exploratory, labelled as such: A1 k-dosing sweep (k in {1, 3, 5}); A3 output-cap doubling; A5 Brier volume check; failure-mode-rate stratification by tier beyond the planned interaction test; any post-hoc tier split of T5.
- Not in scope: cross-model replication; non-English locales; human-in-the-loop variants; cost-savings via model distillation; comparison to non-CoT plan-and-solve prompting families.

## L. Limitations

1. Single-model design. External validity is bounded to the locked model id; the answer may not transfer.
2. Single prompt template. The conclusions are conditional on the Section C template; small prompt-engineering changes beyond the R slot could move the headline.
3. English-only ServiceNow locale. Other locales may have different ax-tree noise characteristics; not measured.
4. Evaluator-LLM bias in failure coding. If a judge LLM is the second coder (Section E), its biases are reported alongside kappa; the primary coder is human.
5. No human-in-the-loop. All actions are model-emitted; request-for-help behavior is not modelled.
6. Task-solving versus generalization. The design measures performance on the benchmark's own tasks; it does not measure generalization to unseen ServiceNow tenants, custom instances, or post-upgrade environments.
7. Source-verifiability. No WorkArena++ task ID, no specific prior-paper success-rate number, and no model version string from outside the supplied workspace is invoked as evidence; every such detail is treated as a researcher-ratified parameter to be locked before execution.

---

## Summary for the Reviewer

This design is a complete, executable, design-only specification for a matched-pairs experiment that asks whether CoT prompting improves LLM-agent task-solving on WorkArena++. With the C0/C1 split as the canonical headline and cost-adjusted success as the co-primary pre-registered alongside it, with Holm-Bonferroni over {H1, H1c, H2, H3}, with paired Wilcoxon tests and bootstrap CIs on delta, with matched-verbosity fillers, a leak-canary, exemplar-pool disjointness, prompt-version pinning, Latin-square ordering, and a 10 percent robustness replication on fresh seeds, the experiment WOULD settle, with pre-registered decision rules per hypothesis in Section A and a pre-registered dominance plot to narrate any success-vs-cost disagreement, whether C1 outperforms C0 on this fixed model and prompt template. Secondary cells C2 (k=3 few-shot) and C3 (N=5 self-consistency at T=0.7) are scored in the same Holm family and pre-registered ablations A1 to A5 dissect the result along prompt-length, exemplar dose, scratchpad, and calibration axes. Every concrete number tied to an unverified assumption (task counts, prompt and input token sizes, exact per-Mtok rates, expected per-trial wall-clock, effective delta detection threshold) is annotated [assumption X / pending confirmation] and is the locked-parameter list that, when finalized, fully specifies execution. No measurement is, or is presented as, observed.
